text: Academic Appeals Policy NSBM Green University handles academic appeals—such as review of assessment results, progression decisions, and final module or degree awards—through structured evaluation and scrutiny boards overseen by its examination and quality assurance divisions. [1, 2] Key Aspects of the Appeal Process • Grounds for Appeal: Generally limited to verified administrative errors, irregularities in examination/assessment conduct, or documented extenuating circumstances (such as severe illness) that impacted performance and were properly reported. [1] • Scrutiny and Review Boards: Assessment results and grading reviews are processed via institutional Scrutiny Boards and Progression and Award Boards to ensure fairness and adherence to standards. [1, 2] • Center for Quality Assurance (CQA): Overall academic standards, quality benchmarks, and policy frameworks are guided by the Center for Quality Assurance and faculty-level quality cells. [1] Contact and Inquiries For specific details on submission deadlines, appeal forms, or department-specific regulations, you can reach out directly: • Hotline: 011 544 5080 • WhatsApp / Mobile: 070 544 5080 • Location: Mahenwatta, Pitipana, Homagama, Sri Lanka • Official Portal / Updates: NSBM Examination Announcements [1] If you can share which faculty or degree program (e.g., Business, Computing, Engineering) you are inquiring about, I can help look up more specific guidelines or contact channels for your department. Results appeals At NSBM Green University, appealing examination or coursework results is managed through the NSBM Examination Department in coordination with your specific faculty and, where applicable, partner universities (such as the University of Plymouth or Victoria University). [1, 2, 3, 4]

1. Valid Grounds for a Results Appeal A result appeal is not a simple re-marking of academic judgment; it is typically only considered on the following grounds: • Administrative or Clerical Error. A miscalculation of marks, missing coursework components, or an error in recording the final grade. • Extenuating Circumstances (EC). Severe medical issues or personal emergencies that affected your exam/assessment performance—provided you submit valid supporting evidence via the NSBM Extenuating Circumstances (EC) Form within the stipulated deadline. • Procedural Irregularity. Evidence that the examination or assessment was not conducted in accordance with NSBM's official regulations. [1, 2, 3] 2. How to Submit an Appeal or Request 1. Check Official Guidelines. Review the NSBM By-Laws and Examination Rules and Regulations on the NSBM Examination Important Documents Portal. [1] 2. Submit Supporting Forms. a. For medical or personal emergencies affecting your results, submit the Extenuating Circumstances (EC) Form along with verified medical certificates or documentation. b. For administrative discrepancies or general grade queries, log in to the NSBM Student Portal under Feedback & Complaint, or submit a formal written request to your Faculty Office and the Examination Division. [1, 2, 3] 3. Pay Applicable Fees. If a formal re-scrutiny or administrative review fee applies to your programme, payments must be completed via the NSBM Examination Online Payment portal. [1] 4. Partner University Degrees. If you are enrolled in an affiliated degree (e.g., Plymouth or Victoria University), your appeal must also follow the partner institution’s specific academic appeal window and regulations after provisional results are released. 3. Direct Contact for Urgent Result Queries Because appeal windows after results release are strictly time-bound, contact the NSBM Examination Department directly for the exact form and deadline for your batch: [1] • Email: examinations@nsbm.ac.lk

• Hotline: 011 544 5080 • WhatsApp: 070 544 5080 • In-Person: Examination Division, NSBM Green University, Mahenwatta, Pitipana, Homagama [1] If you'd like more tailored steps, let me know: • Whether your degree is NSBM-awarded (UGC-approved) or an affiliated foreign degree (e.g., Plymouth, Victoria) • The reason for the appeal (e.g., missing coursework marks, medical emergency, or grade discrepancy)

Academic calendar (semester dates, holidays) NSBM Green University does not use a single university-wide semester calendar; instead, schedules vary by intake batch and affiliated degree partner (such as UGC-approved NSBM degrees, University of Plymouth, or Victoria University). [1, 2, 3] Intake & Semester Structure • Three Annual Intakes. NSBM typically admits undergraduate students across three major cycles each year—February, June, and October. [1, 2, 3] • Batch-Specific Semesters. Each intake (e.g., 26.1, 26.2, 26.3) follows its own 14-to-15-week teaching schedule, study leave, and exam window, managed directly by its respective faculty (Business, Computing, Engineering, or Science). [1, 2] • Partner University Alignment. Programmes offered in affiliation with foreign universities follow the assessment and term timelines set by those partner institutions. [1] Holidays & Campus Closures • Sri Lankan Public & Mercantile Holidays. Academic lectures are generally paused on Sri Lankan statutory public holidays (such as Poya days, Sinhala and Tamil New Year in April, Vesak in May, and Christmas in December), though make- up classes or weekend postgraduate sessions may still be scheduled. [1] • Semester Breaks. Student vacation periods occur between final examinations and the start of the next semester, lasting roughly two to four weeks depending on the batch and degree programme. Where to Check Your Exact Dates • Student Portal & LMS. Log in to the NSBM Student Portal / LMS or check your faculty noticeboard on NFORCE/VLE for your specific batch's semester start, add/drop deadlines, and exam timetables. • Official E-Calendar & Administration. You can view general university announcements on the NSBM Green University Website or contact the academic administration directly at +94 11 544 5000 or inquiries@nsbm.ac.lk. [1]
If you'd like, let me know: • Your intake batch (e.g., 25.2, 26.1, 26.3) • Your faculty or degree partner (NSBM UGC, Plymouth, Victoria, etc.)

Assessment Guideline NSBM Green University structures its assessments through a combination of semester- end written examinations, in-course continuous assessments, and strict quality assurance measures. [1, 2, 3] Key Components of Assessment • In-Course Continuous Assessments: May include classroom tests, take-home assignments, practical tasks, term papers, individual or group presentations, and project reports. [1] • Semester-End Written Examinations: Formal written papers conducted at the end of modules/semesters. [1] • Attendance & Eligibility Requirements: Students are generally required to maintain a minimum attendance threshold (such as 70% in lectures and tutorials depending on the specific faculty or program rules like the NSBM MBA Guide) to remain eligible for sitting exams. [1] Quality Assurance & Moderation • Scrutiny Boards: Review examination papers beforehand to ensure reliability, accuracy, and proper alignment with module learning outcomes. • Marks Moderation: First-examiner marking undergoes a moderation process to maintain fairness and consistency. • External Examiners: Independent academic or industry experts oversee assessment standards and paper quality. [1, 2] Examination Rules & Conduct • Arrival and Seating: Candidates must arrive on time and remain seated for the duration of the examination unless given emergency permission. [1] • Anonymity and Answer Scripts: Writing names or identifiable marks directly on main answer scripts is prohibited. All rough work must be done strictly on provided official paper and handed in. [1] • Academic Integrity: Use of unauthorized materials, communication with other students, or copying leads to strict penalties, including cancellation of results or suspension. [1] Repeat Coursework & Assessments • Students needing to repeat modules or continuous assessments can coordinate through the campus examinations unit or check updates via the NSBM

Examination Repeat Portal. Official inquiries can also be directed to examinations@nsbm.ac.lk. [1, 2] If you want me to look up something more specific, let me know: • Your Faculty or Degree Program (e.g., School of Business, Computing, Engineering) • Whether you are looking for repeat guidelines, medical/absence policies, or assignment formatting rules Assignment and assessment rules NSBM Green University enforces strict rules covering Continuous Assessments (CA), assignment submissions, grading thresholds, and examination conduct. [1, 2] 1. Continuous Assessment (CA) & Grading Rules • Weightage Split: Most modules combine Continuous Assessments (40%– 50%) and a Semester-End Examination (50%–60%), depending on the faculty and degree program. [1, 2] • Minimum CA Threshold: In many programs (such as Business/Management), students must achieve at least 40% in the Continuous Assessment component to be eligible to sit for the final exam. Sitting an exam without meeting CA eligibility can result in voided results. [1] • Overall Pass Mark: To pass a module, students typically need an overall Final Mark of at least 50% (combining CA and exam marks). [1] 2. Assignment Submission & Repeat Rules • Submission Channels: Assignments must be submitted on time through the designated Learning Management System (LMS/NLearn) or physical drop-offs as instructed by the lecturer. • Extenuating Circumstances (EC): If illness or an emergency prevents on-time submission or exam attendance, students must submit an official Extenuating Circumstances (EC) claim with supporting medical/legal evidence under the NSBM Examination Guidelines. [1] • Repeat Coursework: Students who fail a continuous assessment or miss a deadline without valid EC approval must register for repeat coursework, pay the applicable repeat fee, and submit via the faculty-specific links on the NSBM Repeat Assignment Portal. [1, 2]

3. Academic Integrity & Plagiarism • Originality Checks: Written assignments and reports are screened through plagiarism detection software (such as Turnitin). • Zero Tolerance for Collusion: Copying from peers, submitting recycled work without authorization, or using uncredited sources is treated as an academic breach. Penalties range from mark deductions and failing the assignment to disciplinary action by the Examination Board. 4. Written Exam & In-Class Test Rules • Identity & Anonymity: Students must bring their Student ID/Admission Card, but are strictly prohibited from writing their names or identifiable marks on main exam answer booklets. • Rough Work: All calculations and notes must be written only on official stationery provided in the exam hall and attached to the answer script—writing on admission cards or personal papers is treated as attempted cheating. • Legibility: NSBM reserves the right not to grade exam scripts if handwriting is illegible. [1] (Note: For affiliated foreign degree programs—such as Plymouth University or Victoria University—specific late-submission caps and grading rubrics follow the partner university's academic regulations). Are you enrolled in an NSBM UGC-approved degree or a foreign-affiliated program (like Plymouth or Victoria University), and do you need details on a specific rule like late penalties or Extenuating Circumstances?

Attendance policy NSBM Green University generally expects students to maintain a minimum attendance of 75% for lectures, tutorials, and practical/laboratory sessions per module, though exact requirements can vary depending on whether you are following an internal degree program or an affiliated foreign university program (such as UCD, Plymouth, or Victoria University). [1] Key Details of the Attendance Policy • Minimum Requirement: Usually set at 75% of total academic sessions (lectures, tutorials, and labs). [1] • Tracking & Monitoring: Attendance is typically tracked digitally via student ID cards/NFC access control systems or QR code check-ins, and students can monitor their records through the My NSBM App or the NLearn Student Portal. [1, 2, 3] • Impact on Exams: Falling short of the required attendance threshold without valid, approved medical certificates or extenuating circumstances (EC) can result in being barred from sitting for semester-end examinations or losing continuous assessment/participation marks. [1] • Medical / Excused Absences: If you miss classes due to medical reasons or emergencies, you are required to submit valid medical certificates or documentation to your faculty/batch coordinator following the university’s procedure for extenuating circumstances. If you'd like, let me know: • Your specific degree program (e.g., local UGC degree vs. a partner university like Plymouth or UCD) • Which year or semester you are currently in I can give you more tailored details about your specific faculty guidelines.

Course Registration Guideline NSBM Green University provides multiple ways to register for undergraduate, postgraduate, and foundation programs: [1, 2] • Online Registration: Complete your enrollment through the NSBM Online Registration Portal. • On-Campus Registration: Visit the NSBM Green University campus in Homagama to register directly with the guidance of Admissions Officers. • Inquiries & Guidance: Submit a pre-application inquiry via the NSBM FAQ & Support Page if you need help choosing a program or verifying entry requirements. [1, 2] General Entry Requirements • Undergraduate Programs: Usually require 3 simple passes (S) or better in G.C.E. Advanced Level (A/L) examinations in a single attempt, or completion of an approved foundation program. English language requirements typically include a simple pass in A/L General English or an equivalent qualification like IELTS (overall 6.0). [1, 2] • Foundation Programs: Require G.C.E. Ordinary Level (O/L) qualifications (such as 3 to 6 credit passes depending on the specific stream like Science, Engineering, or General Business). [1, 2] • Postgraduate Programs: Require a recognized undergraduate degree or relevant professional experience. [1] You can check out the full lineup of available study tracks on the NSBM Degree Programmes Page. [1] If you'd like, let me know: • Which specific degree or program you are interested in • Your current academic qualifications (A/L, O/L, or pending results) I can give you the exact entry criteria and next steps for that course. Module Selection At NSBM Green University, most degree programs follow a fixed semester structure where core modules are pre-assigned, while optional electives, repeat modules, and LMS enrollments are managed through the student portal. [1, 2]

1. Core vs. Elective Modules • Mandatory Modules. In the early years (Year 1 and Year 2) of most UGC- approved and foreign-affiliated degrees (Plymouth, Victoria University, etc.), your core modules are automatically assigned to your batch by the Faculty Administration. [1] • Elective & Specialization Modules. When you reach specialization semesters (typically Year 2 Semester 2 or Year 3), you will be required to select elective tracks or optional modules based on your chosen major. 2. How to Access & Enroll in Modules • Student Portal & NLearn. Log in to the NSBM Student Portal using your NSBM student email credentials provided upon registration. [1, 2] • LMS Self-Enrollment. Once your semester registration and fee payments are cleared, navigate to your respective Learning Management System (such as NLearn, Plymouth DLE, or VU Collaborate). [1] • Enrollment Keys. Lecturers or department coordinators share module-specific enrollment keys via your student email or during the first week of lectures so you can access module descriptors, timetables, and lecture materials on the LMS. [1] 3. Important Rules & Deadlines • Semester Registration & Payments. You must complete your semester registration and settle the required semester/installment fees before your portal grants access to new module enrollments and exam admissions. • Repeat or Referral Modules. If you need to register for a repeat or referral module from a previous semester, you must submit a repeat exam/module application through the Examinations tab on the NSBM Student Portal before the published deadline. • Add/Drop Window. Changes to elective modules are generally only permitted within the first 1 to 2 weeks of a new semester through your Faculty Admin office. [1] To give you the exact module list or enrollment steps, let me know: • Your faculty and degree program (e.g., Computing, Business, Engineering, or an affiliated university track) • Your current year and semester

EXAMINATION REGULATIONS EXAMINATION REGULATIONS - INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES Name of regulation: Examination Regulations – Instructions to Candidates Purpose of regulation: To instruct students on expectations of their attendance at, and conduct, during examinations Approval for this regulation given by: Academic Governing Council Responsibility for its update: Examinations Unit Regulation applies to: Candidates sitting for any examination conducted Contents 1. Introduction 2. Attendance at Examinations 3. Conduct during Examinations 3. Breaches of Examination Regulations by NSBM Examinations Unit Date of Approval: August 2015 Proposed Date of Review: August 2018

1. INTRODUCTION The objective of this regulation is to make the exa mination candidates aware of the examination rules and regulations applicable to them. All examination candidates are advised to read and understand these regulations and abide by them. It is also the respo nsibility of the examination candidate to make themselves aware of the rules, regulations and how breaches of regulations are handled. 2. ATTENDANCE AT EXAMINATIONS 2.1 Candidates are responsible for making themselves aw are of the date, time and venue for all examinations that candidates are required to take and for presenting themselves at the examination room in good time before the examination is due to begin. 2.2 Candidates shall not enter the examination room unt il instructed to do so by an invigilator. Candidates shall not be admitted to the examination room until ten minutes before the official time of commencement of the examination or of approved reading time, whichever is applicable. 2.3 Candidates shall be admitted to the examination room up to thirty minutes after the official start of the examination, but not normally thereafter. Addit ional time will not be given for any candidate arriving after the start of the examination. Nor sh all a candidate be allowed to leave the hall until after one hour has lapsed from the commencement of the examination. No candidate is allowed to leave before the last 30 minutes of the examination. 2.4 The candidate should have his/her Identity Card and the Admission Card with him/her in the hall on every occasion he/she presents himself for an Exami nation Paper. His/hers candidature is liable to be cancelled if he/she could not produce the Identi ty Card & Admission Card. The candidate shall sign a declaration if he/she fails to produce the Identity Card and produce the Identity card next day. If it is the last day of the examination he shall produce the ID to the Examination Registrar next day. If the candidate has lost the Identity Card a dupli cate should be obtained and produced to the Examination Supervisor. 2.5 Candidates shall not leave the examination room during the first hour or the last thirty minutes of the examination, except in an emergency, where Candidates should seek the prior permission of an invigilator and will be accompanied by the invigilator. 2.6 Candidates must not leave their seating position without the permission of an invigilator. 2.7 If candidate wish to leave the examination room te mporarily, Candidate shall seek the prior permission of an invigilator, and will be accompanied by the invigilator throughout their absence. If

candidate leave the examination room without the pe rmission of an invigilator, candidate will be deemed to have withdrawn from the examination and w ill not be re-admitted to the examination room. 2.8 If candidates wish to leave the examination room early, candidate shall first attract the attention of an invigilator and have their script collected. It is candidate’s responsibility to ensure that candidate script is collected by the invigilator. Candidate must not disturb other candidates when leaving and shall observe examination regulations until out of the room. 2.9 A candidate whose script has been collected shall not be re-admitted to the examination room. 2.10 Any candidate who has registered for an examination can withdraw from the examination within a specific period of time, by submitting a medical ce rtificate from a registered Government Medical Officer at the earliest possible time. 2.11 If a candidate who was registered for a programme could not sit for an examination due to ill health, shall notify it to the Examination Registrar or Cou rse Director immediately within two days with supporting documents. 2.12 A candidate who was absent himself for an examination is not eligible for distinction or merits unless approval is granted by the academic committee. 3. CONDUCT DURING EXAMINATIONS 3.1 Upon entering the examination room candidate must p roduce a valid University registration card (with photograph) to prove candidate’s identity. 3.2 Upon entering the examination room Candidate will b ecome subject to the authority of the invigilators and shall act according to their instructions. 3.3 Candidates shall bring their own pens, calculators, pencils, mathematical instruments, erasers or any other equipment, as requested. 3.4 A mobile ‘phone or any other communication device is not permitted into the examination room. 3.5 Upon entering the examination room Candidates shall place all unauthorized papers, bags, briefcases, mobile phones, calculators, cases, etc., at the point designated by the Supervisor. 3.6 If Candidates bring any unauthorized item to examination hall by mistake candidate must inform an invigilator immediately. Infringement of the University’s regulation includes: o The use of an unauthorized dictionary o The use of other than dedicated calculators with a calculation function only

o The use of unauthorized material stored in the memo ry of a pre programmable calculator, organizer, watch or mobile device o Copying or attempting to copy from another candidate o Leaving the examination room to refer to concealed notes 3.7 If candidates are allowed to bring into the examination room an authorized dictionary or calculator, candidates must ensure that it is first checked by an invigilator. Failure to do so may result in any unauthorized items being removed by the invigilator. 3.8 Candidates shall not commence the examination before being instructed to do so by the Supervisor. 3.9 Candidates shall use only the official examination stationery provided. Any rough work shall be done on the stationery provided and handed in with the completed script. 3.10 Every candidate shall enter his Index Number on the answer book and on every continuation paper. He shall also enter all necessary particulars as indicated in the cover of the answer book. A candidate who inserts an Index Number other than his own numb er is liable to be considered as cheating. A script that bears no Index Number or that bears an Index Number, which cannot be identified, is liable to be rejected. No candidate is permitted to write his name or any other identifiable mark on the answer script. 3.11 All calculations and rough work shall be done on th e papers provided and shall be attached to the answer scripts. Such work should not be done on adm ission card, on timetables or on any other paper. Any candidate who disregards these instructions will be considered as having written notes or outline of answers with the intention of copying. 3.12 Candidates shall not remove any script, rough work, official stationery or other equipment from the room. 3.13 Candidates must write legibly on examination scripts. The University reserves the right not to mark answer script if candidate’s writing is illegible. If, due to a disability, Candidates require special examination arrangements, such as amanuensis suppor t, Candidates must inform the Course director and programme coordinator as soon after en rolment on award as possible and well in advance of any assessment. 3.14 During the examination Candidates shall not communicate in any way with any person other than an invigilator. Any attempt to do so will be considere d as a breach of the University’s Regulations and appropriate action taken. 3.15 If Candidates wish to attract the attention of an invigilator Candidates should do so by raising hand. Candidates shall not leave position without the prior permission of an invigilator.

3.16 Smoking is not permitted in the examination room. 3.17 A small quantity of soft drinks and sweets is permitted to be taken into the examination room. If, in the opinion of the invigilator, these are excessive they will be removed before or during the examination. 3.18 If, in the opinion of the invigilator, candidates c ause an unreasonable disturbance and continue to do so after warning candidates shall be required to leave the examination room and shall not be re- admitted. 3.19 Candidates shall stop writing immediately as instructed to do so at the end of the examination. The Chief Invigilator shall determine the end of the examination. 3.20 At the end of the examination Candidates shall rema in seated and silent until all scripts have been collected and until dismissed by the Supervisor. Ca ndidates may, where permitted, retain examination question papers when they leave the examination. 4. BREACHES OF EXAMINATION REGULATIONS Breaches of Examinations Regulations are treated with utmost seriousness and penalties depend on the seriousness of the offence and can vary from: o A warning to the candidate; o Cancellation of the examination & its results; o Cancellation of the examination & its results and prohibiting the candidate to sit for further examinations at NSBM for a stipulated time period up to three years; o Cancellation of the studentship at NSBM.

text: Exam policy NSBM Green University enforces structured examination regulations managed through its dedicated Examinations Unit and quality assurance framework. [1, 2, 3] Identification and Entry Requirements • Required Documents: Students must carry a valid NSBM Student ID and an official Examination Admission Card to every exam hall. [1] • Missing ID/Admission: Failure to produce them can result in cancellation of candidature, though students may sign a temporary declaration and produce the ID the following day under specific rules. [1] • Arrival & Timing: Candidates must arrive in good time before the paper starts and follow invigilator instructions upon entry. Leaving the hall is generally prohibited during the first and last 30 minutes of an exam. [1] Conduct in the Exam Room • Allowed Items: Only permitted writing instruments, calculators, and specific course-approved equipment are allowed at the desk. • Prohibited Items: Mobile phones, smart devices, smartwatches, bags, and unauthorized papers must be left at the designated storage area designated by the supervisor. Bringing a prohibited device—even by mistake—must be immediately reported to an invigilator. • Behavior: Total silence is required; communicating with other candidates or causing a disturbance leads to disciplinary action. [1, 2] Academic Integrity & Malpractices • Strict Penalties: Copying, plagiarizing, possessing unauthorized study aids or communication devices, or impersonation is treated as a major breach of policy. • Consequences: Offenses can lead to the immediate cancellation of exam results, suspension, or permanent expulsion from the university depending on the severity. [1] Special Circumstances & Quality Assurance • Extenuating Circumstances (EC): Students facing medical emergencies or severe personal issues affecting exams can apply through official Extenuating Circumstances (EC) Guidelines. • Scrutiny and Moderation: All papers undergo a Scrutiny Board review and a marks moderation process by 1st and 2nd examiners supervised by department heads and deans to maintain academic standards. text: Examination Submit no later than 14 working days following the exam date. Claims are reviewed by the EC Board. The EC board will be held after 4 weeks following the last examination date of the relevant semester. EXTENUATING CIRCUMSTANCES GUIDELINES FOR EXAMINATIONS A situation or event that is beyond a student’s control and significantly affects their ability to perform to their full potential during the examination What are Extenuating Circumstances? These circumstances are typically unforeseen, unavoidable, and substantially impact the student's academic performance. When do I apply? What application method should I use? Method: Submission of the EC form with evidence supporting the claim Types of Evidence: Illnesses (Hospitalizations) Significant life events Examples of use: Major accident or injury leading to hospitalization, (whether surgery or not) or any illness affecting a significant period of study, personal or psychological problems for which you are receiving treatment/counselling or have been referred to a counsellor or similarly qualified practitioner, following government advice to self-isolate or otherwise restrict mixing with others, even when asymptomatic or with mild symptoms Death of parent (including step-parents and legal guardian), child, siblings, spouse, parent-in-laws, or grand-parent (only on proof of relationship) Evidence supplied: Diagnosed card, medical reports, Hospital medical certificate. Mentioning the residential treatments, Hospital bill, lab reports. (NOTE: OPD Medical Certificates are not accepted) Death Certificate, Student Birth Certificate, document verifying the relationship with the deceased When to use: Where the student is unable to sit the examination on the day of examination Where the student is unable to sit the examination on the day of examination Valid extenuating circumstances can only be used to gain a fresh attempt for examination and cannot be used to gain additional marks.

text: Types of Evidence Long-term Health conditions Technical issues Examples of use: A long-term health condition is a mental or physical condition that is persistent, typically lasting for more than three months and is often life-long; cannot be resolved in a short time, or which will recur regardless of action, or which needs to be managed on a long-term basis. The following problems will not be approved. • Corrupt data or media • Poor internet connectivity • Printer failure • E-submission of an assessment file in an incorrect format or of the wrong file by accident • Re-submission of an assessment accidentally after the deadline Evidence supplied: A Long-Term Health Condition notification form/card with validated evidence from their healthcare professional The student may submit the relevant evidence to support the claim. When to use: Worsening of ongoing/long-term medical condition where the student is unable to sit the examination on the day of the examination. Applicable for the day of the event that occurred only. (The date/s of the event should match with the date/s of the online examination that the student is unable to complete. Number of EC uses: There is no limit to the number of occasions you can claim extenuating circumstances. If you claim extenuating circumstances many times during your academic period, you will be reviewed, and further action will be taken by the Faculty Administration regarding your academic performance and continuation, (We do expect you to plan your studies to allow for the usual ups-and-downs of life, including minor illnesses or minor personal issues, so claims for extenuating circumstances relating to such minor issues will not be considered) Note for students: Extenuating circumstances claims should be submitted as soon as possible without waiting for 14 days. Incomplete claims (i.e., those lacking either the form or the supporting evidence) will not be considered. Claims submitted after this timeframe will not normally be considered. Students can be assured that all claims of extenuating circumstances are treated as confidential, and any information submitted will be used only to determine the validity of the claim. Submitting false documents or evidence will be considered as an academic misconduct and will be treated separately as an academic offence. Any students found to have submitted fabricated or falsified EC information to the University will be subject to investigation and disciplinary procedures where the standard penalty may even lead to expulsion from the University.
